trace_model.durable_prefix: Commit candidate checkpoint C by CAS against predecessor blob, then exact-read back C before any external-effect attempt.
trace_model.history_no_accept: After exact readback of C, an external-effect attempt is issued but is not accepted before the process crashes; repository state remains C and there is no effect.
trace_model.history_accept_no_ack: After exact readback of C, the same external-effect attempt is accepted and becomes externally visible, but the process crashes before authoritative acknowledgment is durably recorded; repository state is still C.
trace_model.observational_equivalence: At recovery time, repository-only state is identical in both histories: C. Exact pre-effect readback proves only that C committed; it contains no information about which external-effect history occurred.

recovery_impossibility.retry_branch: If recovery retries the external effect from state C, history_no_accept can succeed, but history_accept_no_ack can create a duplicate unless the effect endpoint deduplicates the same durable generation/token.
recovery_impossibility.suppress_branch: If recovery suppresses the retry from state C, history_accept_no_ack avoids duplication, but history_no_accept loses the required effect.
recovery_impossibility.conclusion: No deterministic recovery rule based only on repository checkpoint ordering/readback can guarantee both no omission and no duplicate across the acceptance-before-acknowledgment crash window.

ordering_variants.checkpoint_before_effect: Leaves the two histories observationally equivalent after crash.
ordering_variants.checkpoint_after_ack: Cannot help when the crash occurs after effect acceptance but before acknowledgment/checkpoint update.
ordering_variants.predeclare_attempt_token: Becomes sufficient only if the external effect itself treats that durable token/generation as an idempotency key or exposes authoritative generation-correlated committed-effect visibility; that is an additional primitive, not repository ordering alone.
